items.title: Define the LENS_TO_LANE mapping (six real review lanes per §4.2) + the lane type, in core/adversarial-review-lens-runner.ts
items.context: New module importing S0 (core/adversarial-review.js: LensId, CANONICAL_LENS_SET, Finding). LENS_TO_LANE: Record<LensId, lane> exactly per §4.2 (concept/scope->lattice-review-concept, code-quality->lattice-review-quality, behavior/correctness->lattice-review-behavior, test-coverage->lattice-review-test-coverage, crash-safety/edge->lattice-review-behavior, docs-consistency->lattice-review-docs). The lane type must be the six real review_run_start lanes; pin correctness by cross-checking against review-run.ts REVIEW_RUN_LANES (import it, or assert in the smoke). Every mapped lane must be a real lane.

happy.desc: LENS_TO_LANE has exactly 6 entries, one per LENS_IDS member, with mapped lanes matching spec section 4.2 table (concept/scope->lattice-review-concept, code-quality->lattice-review-quality, behavior/correctness->lattice-review-behavior, test-coverage->lattice-review-test-coverage, crash-safety/edge->lattice-review-behavior, docs-consistency->lattice-review-docs) -> all 6 mappings present and correct; WHY: covers the fundamental mapping correctness that every downstream function depends on

Every value in LENS_TO_LANE is a member of REVIEW_RUN_LANES (imported from core/review-run.ts) -> subset assertion passes; WHY: pins the mapping to reality so a lane rename or removal in review-run.ts is immediately caught

The lane type exported from the module is the union of exactly the six real review_run_start lanes (matches ReviewRunLane from review-run.ts) -> type-level and runtime agreement; WHY: ensures no seventh/phantom lane can be assigned

edge.desc: LENS_TO_LANE has two lenses (behavior/correctness and crash-safety/edge) both mapping to lattice-review-behavior -> both entries present, distinct keys, same value, no collision or overwrite; WHY: the two-to-one mapping is the trickiest part of the table and a naive Set-based uniqueness check would wrongly reject it

LENS_IDS contains slash-form ids (concept/scope, behavior/correctness, crash-safety/edge) used as object keys -> Record lookup by slash-form string succeeds without encoding/escaping; WHY: slash in key is an unusual pattern that could break naive property access

adversarial.desc: If a hypothetical 7th lane were added to REVIEW_RUN_LANES but NOT to LENS_TO_LANE, the subset assertion still passes (LENS_TO_LANE values are a subset, not an exact match) -> no false failure; WHY: verifies the assertion direction is subset-of not equals, which is the correct contract (lattice-review-channel exists in REVIEW_RUN_LANES but is not used by any lens)

If REVIEW_RUN_LANES were to remove lattice-review-behavior, the subset assertion fails because two lenses (behavior/correctness + crash-safety/edge) map to it -> immediate detection of lane drift; WHY: this is the highest-risk drift scenario since two lenses share the lane

items.title: buildLensRunPlan(change, lensSet) -> one INDEPENDENT LensRunRequest per lens (no cross-lens data)
items.context: LensRunRequest = {lensId: LensId, lane, change: string} (the isolated input a lens gets). buildLensRunPlan(change, lensSet=CANONICAL_LENS_SET) returns one request per lens in the (possibly-subset) set, each carrying ONLY the change + its mapped lane — NEVER another lens's findings/outputs (independence, §2.1). Accepts a subset lens set (task-tunable). No behavior beyond plan construction.

happy.desc: buildLensRunPlan(change, CANONICAL_LENS_SET) returns exactly 6 LensRunRequest objects, one per lens in CANONICAL_LENS_SET -> length===6 and each request.lensId is unique across the set; WHY: covers the main-path plan construction

Each LensRunRequest carries exactly {lensId, lane, change} with lane matching LENS_TO_LANE[lensId] and change being the input string -> fields are correct per request; WHY: verifies the request shape matches the contract and the lane lookup works
buildLensRunPlan with default lensSet (omitting the second arg) uses CANONICAL_LENS_SET -> yields 6 requests; WHY: covers the default-parameter path

edge.desc: buildLensRunPlan(change, subsetLensSet) where subsetLensSet contains only 2 of 6 lenses -> returns exactly 2 requests, only for those 2 lenses; WHY: the task-tunable subset is a key spec requirement (section 2.1) and must not silently include extra lenses
buildLensRunPlan(change, emptyLensSet=[]) -> returns empty array (no requests); WHY: degenerate input boundary; an empty set should not crash or produce phantom requests

LensRunRequest does NOT have a findings field or any field carrying another lens output -> Object.keys check on each request yields only {lensId, lane, change}; WHY: independence property (section 2.1) — the request shape must not leak cross-lens data at the structural level

adversarial.desc: buildLensRunPlan called with the same change string for two different subset lens sets -> each call returns requests only for its own subset with no state leakage between calls; WHY: tests that there is no shared mutable state (e.g., a module-level accumulator) across invocations

buildLensRunPlan with a lensSet containing a duplicate lens (same LensDef twice) -> produces at most one request per unique lensId (no duplicate requests); WHY: adversarial duplicate input must not produce duplicate work items that could cause double-counting in downstream aggregation

items.title: runLenses(change, lensSet, runLens) applies the INJECTED per-lens executor + collects per-lane raw Finding[]; collectRawFindings aggregator
items.context: LensRunResult = {lensId, lane, findings: Finding[]} (findings=[] means PASS). runLenses(change, lensSet, runLens: (req: LensRunRequest) => Finding[]) builds the plan, applies the injected runLens to EACH request independently (runLens is the seam for the real review agent; harness/main-agent supplied at MVP), and returns LensRunResult[]. collectRawFindings(results) flattens to Finding[] (+ optionally findingsByLane). Independence enforced: runLens only ever receives a single lens's request, never another's result.

happy.desc: runLenses(change, CANONICAL_LENS_SET, fakeRunLens) where fakeRunLens plants one Finding on concept/scope and returns [] for all others -> returns 6 LensRunResult objects; the concept/scope result has findings.length===1 with the planted Finding; all other 5 results have findings===[] (PASS); WHY: covers the main path of injected-seam execution and per-lens result grouping
collectRawFindings(results) given the above 6 LensRunResults -> returns flat array of length 1 containing exactly the planted Finding; WHY: covers the flattening aggregator main path

runLenses invokes the injected runLens callback exactly once per lens (6 times total for CANONICAL_LENS_SET) -> counter-instrumented fakeRunLens records 6 invocations; WHY: verifies the seam is called per-request, not skipped or double-called

edge.desc: runLenses with a fakeRunLens that returns multiple Findings (e.g., 3) for one lens and [] for the rest -> that lens LensRunResult.findings.length===3, collectRawFindings returns all 3; WHY: multi-finding-per-lens is a realistic scenario (a lens can find several defects)

runLenses with a fakeRunLens that returns Findings for ALL 6 lenses -> all 6 LensRunResults have non-empty findings; collectRawFindings returns the union (total count matches sum of per-lens counts); WHY: no-PASS-lens edge case where every lens finds something
runLenses with a fakeRunLens that returns [] for ALL lenses -> all 6 LensRunResults have findings===[] (all PASS); collectRawFindings returns []; WHY: all-clean edge case

adversarial.desc: The fakeRunLens callback receives ONLY {lensId, lane, change} per invocation — never another lens LensRunResult or another lens request -> instrument fakeRunLens to capture its argument and assert Object.keys match exactly {lensId, lane, change}; WHY: independence is load-bearing (section 2.1); if runLenses leaks prior results into subsequent runLens calls, cross-contamination occurs

Two lenses map to the same lane (behavior/correctness and crash-safety/edge both map to lattice-review-behavior) -> runLenses returns two DISTINCT LensRunResult objects with different lensId but the same lane; fakeRunLens plants a Finding on crash-safety/edge only -> only the crash-safety/edge result has findings, the behavior/correctness result has []; collectRawFindings does not mis-attribute or merge them; WHY: same-lane collision is the highest-risk aggregation bug — findings must stay attributed to their originating lens, not collapsed by lane

fakeRunLens throws an Error for one lens -> runLenses either propagates the error or handles it gracefully (does not silently swallow and return partial results without indication); WHY: a throwing runLens seam simulates a real agent crash; silent swallowing would hide review failures

items.title: Hermetic smoke with a FAKE runLens proving mapping + independence + aggregation; register in lattice.config.json
items.context: New packages/main/src/tasks/adversarial-review-lens-runner-smoke.ts (check+counter pattern). Assert: every value of LENS_TO_LANE is in the real six-lane set (import REVIEW_RUN_LANES from core/review-run.js and assert subset — this PINS the mapping to reality); buildLensRunPlan over CANONICAL_LENS_SET yields 6 requests, one per lens, each with the right mapped lane and carrying only {lensId,lane,change} (no findings field / no cross-lens data); a SUBSET lens set yields only those requests; runLenses with a fake runLens (returns a planted Finding for one lens, [] for others) yields the right LensRunResult[] with findings grouped by lens/lane and PASS lenses empty; collectRawFindings flattens correctly. Register node packages/main/dist/tasks/adversarial-review-lens-runner-smoke.js in lattice.config.json validate.commands.

happy.desc: Hermetic smoke file exists at packages/main/src/tasks/adversarial-review-lens-runner-smoke.ts, uses check+counter pattern, and exits 0 when all assertions pass; WHY: the smoke is the acceptance gate for the entire S1 story

Smoke asserts every value of LENS_TO_LANE is in REVIEW_RUN_LANES (subset check against the real import from core/review-run.ts) -> assertion passes; WHY: pins the mapping to the real lane enum at test time, not just at type-check time

Smoke asserts buildLensRunPlan(change, CANONICAL_LENS_SET) yields exactly 6 requests with correct lensId and lane per request, and no findings field on any request -> all pass; WHY: covers plan construction correctness and independence

Smoke runs runLenses with a FAKE runLens that plants a Finding on one lens and returns [] elsewhere -> asserts correct LensRunResult grouping (findings on the planted lens, empty on others) and collectRawFindings flattens correctly; WHY: end-to-end proof of the injected-seam + aggregation path

Smoke command is registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands as node packages/main/dist/tasks/adversarial-review-lens-runner-smoke.js -> lattice validate runs it; WHY: if not registered, the smoke never runs in CI/validation and is dead code

edge.desc: Smoke tests a SUBSET lens set (e.g., 2 of 6 lenses) via buildLensRunPlan -> asserts only 2 requests returned, only for those 2 lenses; WHY: subset is a spec requirement (task-tunable) and must be exercised in the smoke

Smoke counter tracks total check count and reports it at exit (check+counter pattern) -> final output includes the count of passed assertions; WHY: a smoke that silently passes zero checks is a false-confidence hazard

adversarial.desc: Smoke asserts that when behavior/correctness and crash-safety/edge both map to lattice-review-behavior, they produce SEPARATE LensRunResult entries (distinct lensId, same lane) and findings are not merged or mis-attributed between them -> assertion passes; WHY: the two-to-one lane mapping is the most fragile part of the design; if the smoke does not explicitly test this, a grouping-by-lane bug can ship undetected

Smoke asserts that the FAKE runLens callback never receives a findings field or any prior lens output in its argument -> assertion on request shape passes; WHY: independence is the load-bearing invariant of the lens runner; if the smoke does not explicitly assert the request shape, cross-contamination can ship
